items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: You know, this Louis Barberand living in St. Claude, where they were raised, where they were all raised, I don't know all of them.

ctx.x: Anyway, just one day. Right. Well, first of all, for today.

Okay. What is today? Today's gotta be the 14th. Yesterday was Friday 13th. Friday 13th. You had a good day. November 14th. Okay, fine. And, Mike Delay. Good. From there. We go. One week. Twenty-five years. This time. Next week. Next week. Next, what today is? Saturday? Next Saturday we'll be here. Twenty-five years. From New Orleans. From New Orleans. From New Orleans. That's a lot of time. We're living here twenty-three years, right? You've been here for about fifteen that I know. No, this hour. Twenty-three…
Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: My first job was with Paul Barbaran's youngest brother. He was a drummer. You know, there were three drummers. Lewis, Charles

ctx.x: Is she older or younger than Manuel?

I don't exactly know if she would have been, although Manuel did pass away around 42, 43. I'm not sure what year, but I was somewhere, and I was in the Army, I think it was. Anyhow, and what made me like trumpet or cornet so much is because my mother used to take me there lots of time, visiting when I was a kid. And he was giving lessons, and I just took to the trumpet or cornet. And I always didn't want to play a cornet. So, like I said, she wanted me to play violin, but I didn't like violin. So I went until…
Well, this is Saussure I knew in Chicago, played, Lee Collins played drums. Is that right?
